meta.name: Generate carbon emissions reports with OpenAI, Slack and an ESG dashboard

parameters.content:
## Carbon Emission Monitoring and Reporting

Converts electricity + fuel consumption data into estimated CO2e emissions, classifies the emission level, and generates a periodic sustainability report for management — with human checkpoints for data review and report approval, plus an extra checkpoint if emissions are Critical.

### How to set up
1. Import this workflow into n8n
2. Add credentials: OpenAI (Chat Model) and Slack (chat:write). The two HTTP Request nodes work without credentials against public/demo endpoints — swap in your real carbon-intensity API and ESG dashboard/API and add auth as needed
3. Edit Set - Config: emission factors, thresholds (low/medium/high/critical, in kg CO2e), region, reportingPeriod, notifyChannel, dashboardApiUrl
4. Point the webhook trigger at your metering/facilities data source
5. Point the three Wait nodes' resume webhooks at your review UI's 'acknowledge alert', 'approve data' and 'approve report' actions
6. Activate the workflow, or use the Manual Trigger to test end to end

### How to customize
- Skip the Critical-alert Wait entirely for low-stakes facilities by routing that Switch output straight to Wait - For Data Review
- Change summaryStyle / reportingPeriod in Set - Config (weekly ops digest, quarterly board report, etc.)
- Add a second HTTP Request before Set - Config to pull consumption data automatically from a metering API/database instead of a manual upload
- Swap the Slack node for email, Teams, or generate a PDF via the pdf skill

## 1. Trigger, Config, Grid Factor & Emission Calculation

Set - Config centralizes emission factors, category thresholds, region and reporting settings, and passes through the consumption figures from whichever trigger fired.

HTTP Request - Fetch Grid Emission Factor calls a live carbon-intensity API for the current grid factor (API #1) — continueOnFail is on, so a failed call just falls back to the static factor in Config.

JS - Calculate Carbon Emissions is the first Code node: deterministic math converting kWh + fuel volumes into kg CO2e, plus a low/medium/high/critical category used to route the rest of the flow.

nodes.name: Sticky Note - Routing, Review & Report Generation

parameters.content:
## 2. Emission-Level Routing, Human Review & AI Report

Switch - Emission Level Router sends Critical readings through an extra Wait (acknowledgment) before they rejoin the flow; Low/Medium/High go straight to the standard review checkpoint.

Wait - For Data Review pauses so a person can catch bad meter readings before the AI writes anything — resumed via webhook once the data is approved (as-is or corrected).

IF - Review Approved gates the rest of the flow. On approval, AI - Generate Sustainability Report (LLM chain) writes the executive summary, key metrics, recommendations and tags from the calculated figures.

JS - Parse LLM Output & Build Report Payload safely parses that JSON into the final report fields, falling back to a plain-numbers summary if parsing fails.

## 3. Report Approval & Delivery

Wait - For Report Approval pauses once more before the report goes to management — resumed via webhook when the reviewer hits 'Approve'.

IF - Report Approved gates delivery: approved reports are pushed by HTTP Request - Push Report to ESG Dashboard (API #2) and posted by Slack - Notify Management; declined reports land on Set - Discarded/Cancelled instead. Both delivery nodes use continueOnFail so a delivery hiccup doesn't fail the run.

assignments.name: summaryStyle
assignments.value: executive summary with key metrics, a trend note and 3-5 actionable recommendations
